title: 403 forbidden error on local deployment when creating a custom connector
body:
### What happened?

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fee0c4fb-59a8-4eac-ae66-2b85bf4d2031)

I consistently get errors when trying to create a custom connector locally. I have followed the setup exactly per this guide: https://docs.airbyte.com/platform/using-airbyte/getting-started/oss-quickstart

The issue appears to arise in with requests to /connector_builder/manifest/resolve and as you can see in my browser network requests the manifest and health endpoints on the connector build cause it to break.

I have tried numerous troubleshooting steps including updating Docker Desktop to the latest version, uninstalling and reinstalling abctl and ensuring no other networking issues.

I have also tried various options in the UI, even the most basic YAML input will not work

### What did you expect to happen?

I expect to be able to proceed and create a custom connector here

### Abctl Version

<details>

```console
$ abctl version
version: v0.26.0
```

</details>

comments.author: gomesf
comments.body:
@forrest-dh 

Your commands may vary a little but this should be a rough step by step.
After the "abctl local install" (the 1.7.0) version, I:

1) `kind get clusters` (to get the clusters names)
2) `kind export kubeconfig --name airbyte-abctl` (to make the kind config acessible in kubectl)
3) `kubectl get pods -n airbyte-abctl`(to get the pods names in the airbyte namespace)
4) `kubectl exec -n airbyte-abctl -it airbyte-abctl-webapp-6c59b97f9-dpkwz -- /bin/sh` (to access the pod of the airbyte webapp. PS: This part "6c59b97f9-dpkwz" will be different for you)

Inside the pod:
5) `vi /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf` (edit the file, add the lines in within the server brackets configuration, save and exit)
6) `nginx -s reload` (to reload the nginx)

The thing here is that you should do this in the pod that is running. When/If the pod restarts, the config goes back to the unpatched version and you should do it again.

comments.author: ian-at-airbyte
comments.body:
Hi everyone. Thanks for your patience while we looked into this. I have answers for you.

**What's happening with Helm**

There was an undocumented ingress change in 1.7, and this is what's responsible for the issues with helm deployments. I probably should have caught this earlier, but it just didn't occur to me when I was reviewing what was actually in the version. We initially approached this as a bug, but it's actually a change you'll need to make on your deployment. I'll explain the fix here.

And just to reiterate, [if you're using abctl](https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte/issues/61677#issuecomment-3025191686), this doesn't apply to you at all because it handles ingress on its own, and does so properly in the last patch.

**The fix**

You need to update ingress rules on your deployment to handle `airbyte-server-svc` and `airbyte-connector-builder-server-svc`. Once you do this, the Connector Builder will function normally again in 1.7.1.

We've updated the [release notes](https://docs.airbyte.com/release_notes/v-1.7#patches) to capture this. We've also added updated ingress samples for NGINX and ALB, which are linked from that page ([Self-Managed Community](https://docs.airbyte.com/platform/deploying-airbyte/integrations/ingress), [Self-Managed Enterprise](https://docs.airbyte.com/platform/enterprise-setup/implementation-guide#configuring-ingress)). These should be _fairly_ close to what you end up running but we can't predict what your ingress will look like exactly since everyone's a bit different.

Again, I really do appreciate your patience and understanding. The particular issue discussed here was a poorly-understood consequence of some needed architectural changes that have been happening behind the scenes.

**An example**

For those not too familiar with ingress, here's an overly simplified explanation.

I have a local helm deployment of 1.7.1 in the airbyte namespace, just running on my localhost. Using port forwarding, the Connector Builder did not work (as expected).

**First**, I applied an ingress controller (https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx). For example: `kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/controller-v1.10.1/deploy/static/provider/cloud/deploy.yaml`.

**Then**, I created this file. Yours will probably end up looking different from mine, but the main thing is `airbyte-airbyte-server-svc` and `airbyte-airbyte-connector-builder-server-svc` are handled appropriately. Consult the updated documentation linked above for more examples.

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: airbyte-ingress # ingress name, example: airbyte-production-ingress
  namespace: airbyte
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-redirect: "false"
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules:
    - host: localhost
      http:
        paths:
          - backend:
              service:
                # format is ${RELEASE_NAME}-airbyte-connector-builder-server-svc
                name: airbyte-airbyte-connector-builder-server-svc
                port:
                  number: 80 # service port, example: 8080
            path: /api/v1/connector_builder
            pathType: Prefix
          - backend:
              service:
                # format is ${RELEASE_NAME}-airbyte-server-svc
                name: airbyte-airbyte-server-svc
                port:
                  number: 8001 # service port, example: 8080
            path: /
            pathType: Prefix
```

**Finally**, I applied my yaml file with `kubectl apply -f airbyte-ingress.yaml`.

This ingress setting allowed the Connector Builder to function properly in 1.7.1.

comments.author: justbeez
comments.body:
This requires some translation if you're on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and using the Ingress/Classic Load Balancer pattern on GKE (Standard or Autopilot). At least it did for me.

Our cluster is on GKE Autopilot (Airbyte is deployed via helm) and historically our Classic Load Balancer backend config has pointed to the `airbyte-webapp`—while this has worked across many Airbyte upgrades, I opted to update to it to `airbyte-server` for consistency with the above solution.

**However, these are steps I was able to use to get Connector Builder working again:**
1. Edit the _Service_ for `airbyte-airbyte-connector-builder-server-svc` and add an annotation of `cloud.google.com/neg: '{"ingress": true}'` (this creates an NEG and allows it to be used in ingress rules)
2. Do the same for the `airbyte-airbyte-server-svc` Service (if you haven't already)
3. Edit the existing _Ingress_ object to add the additional backend and its rules (under `spec.rules[].http.paths[]`)
4. Make sure that the attached Classic Load Balancer actually loads the backends and path mappings correctly. In my case, I got an additional NEG-based backend (probably because of my change from `webapp`) so I needed to update the config a bit to get it back in order

That seems to be working for me, so hopefully it'll help others with similar setups.

P.S. would be ideal to have a full GKE write-up in the docs since it's non-trivial to get it to play nicely as it stands today (at least when you're using private clusters and wanting to be able to leverage things like static reserved IP, Google-managed SSL cert, and IAP for auth using Google Accounts).

comments.author: kenske
comments.body:
For those using `oauth2-proxy`, this is what I needed to configure:

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: "airbyte-oauth2-proxy"
data:
  oauth2_proxy.cfg: |
   ...
    reverse_proxy="true"
    upstream_timeout="120s"
    upstreams=["http://airbyte-airbyte-webapp-svc:80", "http://airbyte-airbyte-connector-builder-server-svc:80/api/v1/connector_builder/"]

```

comments.author: bdevlieger
comments.body:
We noticed one other issue that we were not able to resolve yet. It's not crucial, but rather annoying. Everything works if we start from the Airbyte main page, then browse to "Builder" and then open the connection that we want to edit. But when we directly browse to url to edit the connection we get an error:

```
{"message":"Internal Server Error: not yet implemented","exceptionClassName":"java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException","exceptionStack":[],"rootCauseExceptionStack":[]}
```

Least steps to reproduce:
- Open Airbyte
- Go to "Builder"
- [Optional] open one of the connections
- Copy the URL from the URL bar in the browser
- Paste and open the URL in a new tab in the browser

Note that this error happens even _before_ the authentication flow. So when you do this in an incognito tab it immediately shows the error before asking for login details.

Edit: just refreshing the page is already enough to trigger the error.

Edit 2: this error triggers for **any** page on airbyte, even outside of the builder

For 1.7.2 we've planned a more meaningful error message in the UI, with a link to instructions to fix the issue, for anyone that experiences an ingress problem. We've also provided an overview of this in the 1.7 release notes explaining the breaking change and required steps, although I know not everyone reads those.

This did spur some conversation about alternative options. Not yet sure if that will amount to anything, but there's an appetite to improve the overall UX around deployments.

comments.body:
@Nettorino Thanks for the report.

There were a couple of issues with charts and images. Yours was one of them. The fix is patchless. However, you will need to pull Airbyte images again. I ran `abctl local uninstall` followed by `abctl local install`. I can get credentials and use the Connector Builder as expected.
